extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, legal researchers, and policy watchers interested in major pharmaceutical litigation/settlements
extracted.subtask_description: A chronological/table list of the largest monetary settlements between the U.S. Department of Justice and pharmaceutical companies, summarizing year, company, total settlement, alleged violations, products involved, and statutes violated; intended as a reference/resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion scope (which settlements are listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is a list of the 20 largest settlements reached between the United States Department of Justice and pharmaceutical companies from 2001 to 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only settlements between the DOJ and pharmaceutical companies are considered; the list is limited to the top 20 by total settlement amount for the stated period (2001–2013). Entries are drawn from cited DOJ announcements and news sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering criterion (how entries are ranked)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordered by the size of the total settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranking uses the total settlement amount (see 'Settlement amount composition' for what is included in that total).

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement amount composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement amount includes both the civil (False Claims Act) settlement and criminal fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts reported combine civil and criminal components where applicable (examples: Glaxo's $3 billion = $1B criminal + $2B civil; Pfizer’s listed $2.3B included a record-breaking $1.3B criminal fine). When available, the page notes the criminal vs civil split and later adjustments or different-year valuations (e.g., inflation-adjusted figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Year
rubrics_metrics.description: The calendar year associated with the settlement (as presented in the table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to situate the settlement historically; entries list the year the settlement was announced or recorded in the sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company
rubrics_metrics.description: The pharmaceutical company (or companies) that agreed to the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company names often link to Wikipedia articles and are footnoted to primary sources (DOJ press releases, news coverage). Parent companies or merged entities may be noted (e.g., formed by merger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation(s) — allegation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The alleged unlawful conduct leading to the settlement (e.g., off-label promotion, kickbacks, Medicare/Medicaid fraud, poor manufacturing practices, misclassification under rebate programs, monopolistic practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations are summarized as categories in the table; the page also provides context (e.g., Franklin v. Parke-Davis as first federal recognition of off-label promotion as an FCA violation). Specific allegations are sourced to DOJ announcements and news reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product(s) involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific drugs or products that were the focus of the allegations and settlements (e.g., Avandia, Wellbutrin, EpiPen, Oxycontin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, the table lists one or more products tied to the misconduct; this helps link the legal allegation to particular marketed products or uses (e.g., promotion of pediatric use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laws/statutes violated
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific federal statutes or regulations cited as violated (e.g., False Claims Act, FDCA, Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, Prescription Drug Marketing Act, FDA Current Good Manufacturing Practices, Anti-Kickback Statute, Medicaid Rebate Statute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table records the legal basis for civil/criminal action as reported by DOJ and other sources; multiple statutes may be listed for a single settlement. These entries allow readers to see legal theories used in major enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing/citation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Each settlement entry is supported by references to DOJ press releases, news articles, or corporate announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries include footnotes linking to primary sources (justice.gov, nytimes, archived DOJ PDFs, company press releases). The page emphasizes documentary sourcing for each listed settlement and provides reference details for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable legal context / precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual legal notes that explain significance (for example, Franklin v. Parke-Davis recognizing off-label promotion as an FCA violation; record-setting fines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights precedents and historically significant aspects of particular settlements (e.g., record civil FCA settlement, first recognition of a legal theory), which help interpret why certain settlements are notable beyond dollar amount.
